The Scriptorium

Blessed Are the Ball-Playing Centre-Backs

A book of proverbs for defenders who bring the ball out from the back as if it were an offering.

Posted 11 January 2026 · Proverbs · A 5-minute sermon

And seeing the tactics boards, the Rev. opened his mouth and taught them, saying: blessed are the meek of touch, for they shall inherit the half-space. For of old it was said unto the defender, clear thy lines, and ask questions later; but I say unto you, receive the ball upon the half-turn, look up as one who expecteth good news, and pass through the lines as a hot knife through margarine. The goalkeeper is not thy bomb bay; he is thy eleventh believer.

The 3-5-2 Summary

  • The hoof is dead; build-up is risen. The centre-back is now the chapel's first reader.
  • Eight beatitudes follow, one for each virtue of the ball-playing defender.
  • Progressive passing is prophecy: seeing the run before the runner has run it.
  • With great elegance cometh great accountability — one heavy touch and thou art a meme.

The Beatitudes of the Back Line

Wisdom crieth aloud in the penalty area; she raiseth her voice at the edge of the box.

Blessed are the calm in possession, for they shall not pass back to a goalkeeper who standing like a mannequin of sorrow.

Blessed are those who receive on the half-turn, for theirs is the kingdom of the forward pass.

Blessed are the left-footed, for they shall open angles the right-footed knew not of.

Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after progressive carries, for they shall break the first line and be filled.

Blessed are the merciful, who step out to intercept yet leave a covering shadow, for they shall obtain defensive transition.

Blessed are the pure of first touch, for they shall see through the press as through a glass window.

Blessed are the peacemakers, who take the ball off a panicking full-back and slow the very pulsing of the match.

Blessed are those who are persecuted for the outswinging diagonal, for theirs is the applause of the away end and the highlight reel.

Woe Unto the Hoofers

The letter killeth; the diagonal giveth life.

But woe unto you, disciples of the agricultural clearance, defenders of the if-in-doubt orthodoxy — for the press hath studied your hoof, and the second ball falleth unto the enemy as rain upon the just and the unjust alike. Woe also unto the over-trusting, the dweller-upon-the-ball, the centre-back who attempteth the Cruyff turn upon his own six-yard box: for your punishment shall be swift, televised, and looped forever. There is a fine line between the libero and the liability, and that line is called timing.

Every great defence begins as an act of creation: first the ball, then the world.

Consider the numbers as one considereth the lilies: in the great leagues of Europe, the average centre-back now completes more passes in a season than many a number ten of old. The game has been baptised, and the defence has become the first attack. Rejoice, therefore, and be exceedingly glad — for great is your xG buildup in heaven.

May your half-turns be smooth, your diagonals measure forty yards on the dot matrix of destiny, and your clearing headers travel only when they are truly necessary. Amen. And may you never be nutmegged near your own area.

The Rev. Crossbar plays centre-back at walking pace, which he describes as "deep-lying libero" and his teammates describe as "please just kick it."
